data.name: Vitransh
data.gender_notes: Vitransh is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Vitransh is a combination of two Sanskrit words - 'Vitra' which means to conquer or destroy and 'Ansh' which means essence or form. This name is believed to bring courage, strength and victory to the one who bears it. The name Vitransh carries the meaning “Brave, Victorious” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Hindu tradition and is also used in Sanskrit, Hindi. Parents who choose Vitransh usually hope their child will grow to embody brave, victorious and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Vitransh is a powerful name that resonates with the divine energy of the universe. It is believed to bring success, prosperity and protection to the one who wears it.
data.etymology: Vitransh belongs to the Hindu linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Brave, Victorious.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Vitransh total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.

historical_references.reference: Vitransh is mentioned in the Mahabharata, an ancient Sanskrit epic, as the name of a king who ruled over Hastinapura. He is the father of Bhishma, who is known for his vow to remain unmarried and dedicate his life to protecting the Kuru dynasty.
historical_references.context: Mahabharata is one of the two major Sanskrit epics of ancient India, the other being the Ramayana. It is a significant text in Hinduism, Jainism, and Buddhism, and has been a major influence on the cultures of the Indian subcontinent.

historical_references.reference: Vitransh is also mentioned in the Puranas, a set of eighteen sacred texts in Hinduism. He is described as the son of Vibhishana, the minister of Ravana in the epic Ramayana. Vitransh is said to have performed severe penance to please Lord Shiva and was granted the boon of having a son who would be a great warrior and a venerable sage.
historical_references.context: The Puranas are a significant source of Hindu mythology, philosophy, and religious practices. They provide detailed accounts of the gods and goddesses, heroes and sages, and various aspects of Hinduism.
